posts.body_html:
First time ever getting this tuberous sundew to flower! It sulks year after year but hasn't died. It hasn't ever produced an extra tuber either! GOSH! This is the first time it is looking really good, I've been growing all of my tuberous sundews exclusively outdoors because I want to figure out how to do it. No doubt, without climate control it is extremely challenging but not impossible!

Can anyone ID the species?










These are from February 2024. This one was labeled D. auriculata Bathurst, NSW, can anyone confirm the ID? This is my favorite "common" tuberous sundew ever, it produces enormous, study plants that don't fall over and doesn't seed everywhere till kingdom come. It doesn't go dormant instantly like the rosetted tuberous sundews when exposed to heat, but it will eventually go dormant early if kept too warm for too long:








Some D. menziesii, best beginner type tuberous sundew:
